# Module `operations` of graph `example_graph`

Prefix `ops`, version 1.0.0. How work gets done, the processes, the instructions and policies that govern them, the trainings roles need and the tasks people carry out; not the structure of the company (organization) or the people (people).

Ontology `company` 1.1.0. The live source is `graph describe module operations --graph example_graph --json`; it wins when they differ. Fields, states and relations of a type: `graph describe type <type> --graph example_graph --json`.

## Types

| Type | Alias | Abstract | Extends | Names | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ops:Instruction` | `INSTR-0001` | no |  | `title` (main name), `alt_labels` (other names) | A written how-to for carrying out one process, the prescription of the steps. |
| `ops:Policy` | `POL-0001` | no |  | `title` (main name), `alt_labels` (other names) | A binding rule of the company that applies to units and governs processes; unlike an instruction it says what must hold, not how to do it. |
| `ops:Process` | `PROC-0001` | no |  | `name` (main name), `alt_labels` (other names) | A recurring way of getting one kind of work done, owned by a position. |
| `ops:Task` | `TASK-0001` | no |  | `title` (main name) | One concrete piece of work, usually an occurrence of a process, handed to a person. |
| `ops:Training` | `TRN-0001` | no |  | `title` (main name), `alt_labels` (other names) | A course or certification that the carriers of a role complete. |
